Saturday 7 Nov

Sea Bass, Garlic Butter and Crushed Potatoes with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes

Fish40 min

Ingredients

Sea bass and butter
  • Sea bass fillets440 g
  • Garlic4 cloves
  • Fresh parsley13 g
  • Salted butter85 g
  • Capers25 g (about 2¾ tbsp)
  • Salt½ tsp
  • Vegetable oil¾ tbsp
Side
  • Potatoes750 g
  • Salt¾ tsp
  • Cherry tomatoes210 g
  • Olive oil¾ tbsp
  • Vegetable oil1¾ tbsp

Method

  1. Boil potatoes. Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Chop the potatoes into bite-sized pieces and boil in salted water 15–20 min until tender. Drain and leave to steam dry in a colander.
  2. Roast tomatoes. Put the whole cherry tomatoes on a large tray, drizzle with olive oil, shake to coat and roast 25 min.
  3. Prep. Mince the garlic. Finely chop the parsley.
  4. Make garlic butter. Melt the butter with the garlic over medium-low heat. Cook 1 min, add the parsley and capers and cook 1–2 min more without burning. Set aside.
  5. Roast potatoes. Spread the potatoes on a second tray, drizzle generously with oil, crush with a fork and season. Bake on the top shelf 20 min until crisp.
  6. Fry sea bass. Pat the fillets dry and salt the skin. Fry skin-side down in a little oil over medium-high heat for 4 min until crisp, flip and cook 1 min more. Serve with the potatoes and tomatoes, drizzled with the garlic butter.

Boil the potatoes ahead of time: the cooler they are before roasting, the crispier they get.

Sunday 8 Nov

Pasta alla carcerata (sausage, tomato and cream pasta)

PastaTime not givenServes 6.5

Amounts are for 6.5 servings: the recipe's 2.5 servings × 2.6. The recipe has no written steps, so the method below is the planner's, not the creator's.

Ingredients

Pasta (6.5 servings)
  • Mezze maniche or rigatoni520 g
  • Pork sausage455 g
  • Onion1⅓ medium
  • Tomato passata390 ml (about 1⅔ cups)
  • Cooking cream286 ml (about 1¼ cups)
  • White wine or brandy156 ml (about ⅔ cup)
  • Parmesan or Grana104 g
  • Parsley1 large bunch
  • Olive oil78 to 104 ml (5 to 7 tbsp)
  • Saltto taste

Method

  1. Finely chop the onion and parsley. Remove the sausage casing and crumble the meat.
  2. Soften the onion in the olive oil over medium heat, about 5 minutes.
  3. Add the sausage, break it up and brown it, about 5 to 7 minutes.
  4. Add the wine or brandy and let it bubble until the smell of alcohol has gone.
  5. Add the passata and a pinch of salt. Simmer on low heat about 10 minutes.
  6. Cook the pasta in salted water.
  7. Stir the cream into the sauce and warm it through.
  8. Drain the pasta and toss it in the sauce, with a little pasta water if needed. Off the heat, stir in the Parmesan and parsley.

Monday 9 Nov

Express: Black Pepper Beef and Edamame Rice

Red meat20 min

Ingredients

Beef
  • Steak strips440 g
  • Baking soda6 g (1 tsp)
  • Corn starch13 g (2 tbsp)
Stir-fry
  • Black pepper sauce75 g (about ¼ cup)
  • Soy sauce19 ml (1¼ tbsp)
  • White sugar6 g (1½ tsp)
  • Rice vinegar19 ml (1¼ tbsp)
  • Ginger-garlic paste13 g (2½ tsp)
  • Oyster sauce25 g (1½ tbsp)
  • Sweet soy sauce19 ml (1¼ tbsp)
  • Sliced green beans130 g
  • Sliced pepper130 g
Rice
  • Cooked basmati rice380 g
  • Edamame beans130 g
To serve
  • Sesame seeds6 g (2 tsp)
From your pantry
  • Vegetable oil, olive oil, salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Marinate. Mix the steak strips with baking soda, corn starch, a drizzle of vegetable oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside.
  2. Make sauce. Combine the black pepper sauce, soy sauce, sugar, rice vinegar, ginger-garlic paste, oyster sauce and sweet soy sauce.
  3. Fry. Heat a large pan over high heat with a little oil. Fry the steak for 3–4 min until browned and caramelised, then set aside. Add a little more oil and fry the green beans and peppers for 2–3 min until charred and softened.
  4. Warm rice. In another pan, heat a drizzle of oil. Break up the rice, add it with the edamame and a pinch of salt and pepper, and fry 2–3 min until hot.
  5. Add sauce. Return the beef to the pan with the sauce and stir-fry 2–3 min until thickened.
  6. Serve the beef with the edamame rice, topped with sesame seeds.

Baking soda is what makes the beef tender. A little goes a long way.

Tuesday 10 Nov

Smoky Chicken with Sundried Tomato Mash and Zesty Green Veg

Chicken40 minKid-friendly

Ingredients

Smoky chicken
  • Skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs630 g
  • Smoked paprika5 g (2 tsp)
  • Cumin powder3 g (1¼ tsp)
  • Garlic powder3 g (1¼ tsp)
  • Dried thyme3 g (about 2¼ tsp)
  • Salt¼ tsp
  • Black pepper¼ tsp
  • Olive oil¾ tbsp
Sundried tomato mash
  • Potatoes630 g
  • Sun-dried tomatoes75 g
  • Butter13 g
  • Grated Parmesan55 g
  • Whole milk130 ml (about ½ cup)
  • Salt¼ tsp
  • Black pepper¼ tsp
Green veggies
  • Broccoli250 g
  • Lemon1
  • Green peas130 g
  • Lemon pepper seasoning5 g (2 tsp)
From your pantry
  • Vegetable oil, olive oil, salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Prep. Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put a pot of salted water on to boil. Cut the broccoli into florets, peel and chop the potatoes, finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes. Zest the lemon (avoid the white pith) and cut it into quarters.
  2. Make mash. Boil the potatoes 20 min until soft, drain, then mash with the butter, milk, Parmesan, salt and pepper. Stir in the sun-dried tomatoes.
  3. Marinate chicken. Mix the smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder, thyme, a squeeze of lemon, salt, pepper and a drizzle of oil; toss the chicken in it.
  4. Roast chicken 20–25 min until crisp and cooked through.
  5. Boil veg. Boil the broccoli and peas in salted water 3 min. Drain and toss with the lemon pepper seasoning and lemon zest.
  6. Serve the chicken on the mash with the green veg.

For kids: keep back some plain chicken, plain mash and plain broccoli and peas.

Wednesday 11 Nov

Sweet Potato and Black Bean Quesadillas with Guacamole

Vegetarian30 min

Ingredients

Quesadilla
  • Sweet potatoes500 g
  • Red onion1
  • Garlic1 clove
  • Black beans300 g
  • Black pepper1¼ tsp
  • Salt1¼ tsp
  • Olive oil1¼ tbsp
  • Vegetable oil1¼ tbsp
  • Tomato paste90 g (6 tbsp)
  • Taco seasoning13 g (1¾ tbsp)
  • Chipotle powder3 g (1¼ tsp)
  • 8" tortilla wraps5
  • Vegan mozzarella95 g
Guacamole
  • Fresh coriander19 g
  • Avocado1
  • Lime2½
  • Salt½ tsp
From your pantry
  • Vegetable oil, olive oil, salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Prep. Peel and chop the sweet potatoes. Finely slice the red onion and garlic. Drain and rinse the beans. Chop the coriander.
  2. Make mash. Boil the sweet potatoes in salted water 12–14 min until soft. Drain, add a good drizzle of olive oil and mash; season.
  3. Make chilli. Fry the onion in a little oil with a pinch of salt for 5 min. Add the garlic, taco seasoning (spicy) and a pinch of chipotle (spicy) for 1 min. Add the tomato paste and beans and cook 2 min. Season.
  4. Make guacamole. Mash the avocado with lime juice until smooth; season and top with coriander.
  5. Assemble. Spread sweet potato mash over half of each tortilla, top with bean chilli and a handful of mozzarella, and fold into a half moon.
  6. Fry quesadillas in a little oil over medium heat 3–4 min, pressing down, then flip and cook 3–4 min more until crisp. Repeat. Serve with the guacamole.

When flipping, slide the spatula in at the open side so the folded side stays on the pan.

Thursday 12 Nov

Minestrone Soup with Chicken

SoupAbout 45 min1 mirepoix cube

Ingredients

Soup
  • Cannellini beans, soaked or tinned1 cup
  • Chicken legs3
  • Zucchini1
  • Green beans1 handful
  • Crushed tomatoes1 quart (about 950 ml)
  • Chicken bone broth2 cups (about 480 ml)
  • Mirepoix cube, from the freezer1
  • Olive oil, salt, pepper, fresh herbs to finish

Method

  1. Pan-fry the chicken legs in olive oil over medium-high heat until browned. Remove from the pan.
  2. Chop the vegetables into bite-sized pieces and sauté in the chicken fat with salt and pepper, about 3 min until slightly browned.
  3. Add the mirepoix cube, chicken legs, beans, tomatoes and broth; season.
  4. Cover and simmer 30 min, until slightly reduced and the chicken comes off the bone.
  5. Remove the bones, check the seasoning and finish with fresh herbs.

Friday 13 Nov

Tuna spaghetti with capers, olives and sun-dried tomatoes

PastaTime not given

Ingredients

Pasta
  • Spaghetti alla chitarra200 g
  • Tuna fillets140 g
  • Garlic1 small clove
  • Capers1 tsp
  • Taggiasca olives40 g
  • Sun-dried tomatoes in oil40 g
  • Olive oil30 ml (2 tbsp)
  • Salt, pepper, parsley, zest of ½ lemon

Method

  1. Cook the spaghetti in plenty of lightly salted boiling water.
  2. Drain the sun-dried tomatoes well and slice into thin strips.
  3. In a pan over low heat, soften a crushed garlic clove with the rinsed capers, olives and tomatoes in a generous glug of oil.
  4. After a couple of minutes add the well-drained tuna and stir gently.
  5. Add two ladles of pasta water for a creamy base.
  6. Drain the pasta very al dente and add it straight to the pan. Toss over medium heat, adding more pasta water only if needed.
  7. Off the heat, finish with black pepper, chopped parsley and grated lemon zest.
